one_liner: Header-only PATRICIA/radix-tree map beating std::map on insert/contains for string and numeric keys.
what_it_does: RadixMap is a sorted associative container for std::string or integral/floating-point keys, exposing insert/contains/at/operator[]/erase/find/lower_bound/upper_bound and ascending-order iteration much like std::map. It adds prefix_range(prefix), a bounded-descent query for every key starting with a prefix, which std::map has no clean way to express. It is not a drop-in template-for-template swap: no comparator/allocator parameter, and any Key beyond std::string or arithmetic types needs a RadixMapKeyTraits<Key> specialization.
how_it_is_fast: Uses a PATRICIA/radix-tree structure that stores each shared key prefix once per node (a node for "http://" is shared by every key starting with it) instead of comparing whole keys node-by-node like a red-black tree, and branches via an adaptively-sized bit-mask over the next byte rather than per-byte/per-key comparison. Nodes and values are allocated from a block-based bump/arena allocator (RadixMapArena) rather than individually. For fixed-length keys (integral/floating-point), the find()/lower_bound() traversal stack is backed by the vendored BoundedVector, making that state heap-allocation-free.
when_to_use: Sorted map over std::string or integral/floating-point keys where insert/contains throughput matters most: 3.2x/5.4x faster than std::map for strings, 2.2x/2.3x for doubles at 20,000 keys (Release, -O3, per README).
Need prefix search over string keys (prefix_range) instead of hand-rolling lower_bound() plus an increment-last-byte upper bound that breaks on a 0xFF-terminated prefix.
Workload dominated by contains()/at()/operator[] rather than find()/lower_bound(): contains() is far cheaper than find() in the same benchmarks (e.g. ~70-73ms vs ~452-461ms for 20,000 string keys).
Single-threaded or externally-synchronized use only — no built-in thread safety.
C++20 codebase willing to vendor two header files (RadixMap.hpp + BoundedVector.hpp) rather than link a library.
when_not_to_use: Need reverse iteration: no rbegin()/rend()/operator--, forward-only because the tree has no parent pointers.
Need a custom comparator or allocator template parameter — the header's own doc comment lists both as unsupported.
Erase-heavy workloads: erase() is a tombstone that clears the value but leaves the compressed tree structure (and its memory) untouched, so memory grows with churn beyond the live entry count.
Key type has no RadixMapKeyTraits specialization and you don't want to write one (only std::string and arithmetic types are built in).
Risk-averse selection: 0 GitHub stars, first commit 2026-07-06, single author, 0 issues opened yet, no independent benchmarking or production use documented.

integration.dependencies: none at runtime; Catch2 3 is required only to build/run the bundled RadixMap-test.cpp benchmark/test suite; optional integration with a separate Ensure.hpp project for throw_if(), falls back to an equivalent local implementation if that header isn't present
integration.platforms: no explicit architecture requirement documented; CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) builds and tests on ubuntu-24.04 and macos-latest via CMake+Ninja; Windows/MSVC not covered by CI
integration.thread_safety: not thread-safe — the class's own doc comment explicitly lists 'thread-safety' under 'Not supported'
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — explain: same core operations as std::map (insert/contains/at/operator[]/erase/find/lower_bound/upper_bound/iteration) but no comparator/allocator template parameter, requires a RadixMapKeyTraits<Key> specialization for any Key beyond std::string/arithmetic types, and needs a second vendored header (BoundedVector.hpp) despite the repo description calling it single-header

gotchas: Range-for needs auto&& or auto, never auto&: operator*() returns a proxy Entry{Key first; Value& second;}, not a reference into a stored pair, so 'for(auto &entry : map)' fails to compile.
+0.0 and -0.0 double keys encode to different byte patterns and are treated as distinct, unlike std::map<double,...>'s default std::less which treats them as equal.
erase() does not reclaim compression: repeated insert/erase churn leaves memory usage above the current live-entry count, with no compact() available yet.
prefix_range() degenerates to at most a single entry for fixed-width key types like double, since a shorter double isn't itself a valid key — it only does useful prefix work for std::string keys.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick RadixMap over the B-tree-family siblings (fast-containers, Flat-Map-RB-Tree, cpp-btree, frozenca/BTree, tlx::btree_map) when you specifically need prefix_range()-style prefix queries over std::string keys, or want a two-header vendor-and-go dependency rather than a library benchmarked at multi-million-element scale. Pick libart instead if you want a more independently scrutinized adaptive radix tree (with a C API, not a std::map-like C++ interface); pick a B-tree sibling if you need comparator/allocator customization or verified performance at 1M+ elements, since RadixMap has only been measured at 20,000 keys by its sole author.
verified_claims_summary: README's Catch2 [benchmark]-tagged test cases (Release build, -O3, compiler version and CPU unstated), inserting and then contains()-checking 20,000 keys, report RadixMap 3.2x faster insert and 5.4x faster contains() than std::map for std::string keys (~111-118ms/~70-73ms vs std::map's ~366-369ms/~379-407ms), and 2.2x faster insert / 2.3x faster contains() for double keys (~101-104ms/~46-47ms vs std::map's ~215-234ms/~100-109ms).
status_note: Active but very new (first commit 2026-07-06, last commit 2026-07-09), single-author, 0 stars, 0 issues opened; Apache-2.0 licensed and header-only (two files: RadixMap.hpp + BoundedVector.hpp), trivial to vendor or drop.
